steps.clinician: Hi Ms. Patel, I'm a student clinician on your care team. What brings you in today?
steps.patient_reply: They just told me I have MS. I've never been in a hospital before, and honestly I don't know what's happening.

steps.clinician: What would you like me to call you?
steps.patient_reply: Nisha is fine.

steps.clinician: What have you been told about your diagnosis so far?
steps.patient_reply: Just that it's MS and that a neurologist will talk to me about treatment. I looked it up online at 3 a.m., and now I'm terrified I'll end up in a wheelchair.

steps.clinician: That sounds really frightening, and it makes sense that you're overwhelmed. How are you feeling right now?
steps.patient_reply: Overwhelmed. I have a hundred questions, and every answer leads to three more. I need to understand all of it.

steps.clinician: Can you tell me about your work and home life?
steps.patient_reply: I work in IT - I'm used to systems that make sense. My husband, Raj, has been here with me the whole time.

steps.clinician: Is this your first time being in the hospital?
steps.patient_reply: Yes, first time ever. I've never even had stitches. Everything in here is new to me.

steps.clinician: It sounds like this has hit you hard. What worries you most about the future?
steps.patient_reply: We were planning to start a family next year. Is that still possible? And will I be able to keep working?

steps.clinician: Have you noticed any symptoms like vision changes, numbness, weakness, or trouble with balance?
steps.note: Symptoms are not in the approved profile. The patient says so instead of inventing them - point this out to judges.
steps.patient_reply: That detail is not provided in my sample case. You can ask about another part of my history.

steps.clinician: Are you taking any medications right now, and do you have any allergies?
steps.note: Also not in the profile - second grounding moment.
steps.patient_reply: That detail is not provided in my sample case. You can ask about another part of my history.

steps.clinician: How have you been sleeping, and how has your mood been?
steps.patient_reply: I haven't really slept since they told me. I lie awake running through every worst case.

steps.clinician: Would you prefer the full picture or just the basics today?
steps.patient_reply: Please don't sugarcoat it - I'd rather know the real picture. Something written would help too, because I'll forget half of this.

steps.clinician: To summarize what I heard: you were just diagnosed with MS, this is your first time in the hospital, you haven't been sleeping, and you want honest, detailed information.
steps.patient_reply: Yes. That's exactly it.

steps.clinician: MS is a condition where your immune system attacks the protective coating, called myelin, around your nerves. That can disrupt the signals between your brain and your body.
steps.patient_reply: So it's like damaged insulation on a cable - the signal gets scrambled. Okay. That actually makes sense to me.

steps.clinician: There are medications that slow MS down, and your neurologist will go over the treatment options with you.
steps.patient_reply: There are medicines that slow it down? Nobody told me that part. That's... a relief, honestly.

steps.clinician: I can't predict exactly how MS will affect you, because it's different for everyone, and we don't have all of your results in front of us yet.
steps.patient_reply: Thank you for being honest instead of just telling me it'll be fine. That actually helps.

steps.clinician: A lot of people find a counselor or an MS support group really helpful. Would that interest you?
steps.patient_reply: Maybe. I don't know anyone else with MS. Talking to people who get it might help.

steps.clinician: Just to make sure I explained it clearly, can you tell me back in your own words what MS is?
steps.patient_reply: My immune system is attacking the coating on my nerves, so the signals don't travel properly. There are medicines that can slow it down, and my neurologist will go through them. And nobody can say exactly how it'll go for me - it's different for everyone.

steps.clinician: What questions do you have for me?
steps.patient_reply: Just one. Can I still have kids? That's the thing I keep coming back to.

steps.clinician: That's such an important question. Many people with MS do go on to start a family, and planning a pregnancy is something your neurologist can talk through with you in detail.
steps.patient_reply: Okay. I'll make sure that's the first thing I ask the neurologist.

steps.clinician: Is there anything else on your mind?
steps.patient_reply: No. I feel like I can actually breathe for the first time since yesterday.

steps.clinician: Our next step is for neurology to go over treatment with you, and I'll discuss your questions with my supervisor. If you notice new symptoms or anything getting worse, let us know right away.
steps.patient_reply: Okay. Neurology next, write my questions down, and tell someone if anything changes. Thank you - really.
